findings.pdf_says: Format 1 (to-message-server): 'SEND TO { literal-1 / message-server-name-1 } FROM identifier-1' -- at 300 dpi (crop of the printed glyphs, and again for Format 2 'SEND TO  data-name-2  FROM identifier-1') the underline rule runs only beneath SEND and beneath FROM. There is a clear gap after the D of SEND and NO rule beneath TO in either format. (By contrast the SET formats on pp. 759-762 do print an underline beneath TO, so the omission here is deliberate typesetting, not a printing defect.)
findings.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md line 30641 (Format 1 figure note): '... Underlined (required) words: SEND, TO, FROM, RETURNING, EXCEPTION, NOT, END-SEND.'  and line 30658 (Format 2 figure note): '... Underlined (required) words: SEND, TO, FROM, RAISING, EXCEPTION, LAST, NOT, END-SEND.'
findings.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2 an underlined word is a REQUIRED word; a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word that may be omitted without changing meaning. Both SEND figure notes promote the optional word TO to required. A compiler implemented from this transcription would reject legal source such as SEND "SRV" FROM WS-MSG RETURNING WS-TAG ... END-SEND (TO omitted) -- the same falsely-restrictive direction as the known choice-indicator losses. The choice-indicator bars and every other claim in these two notes are correct; only the TO entry is wrong.
findings.suggested_repair: In both figure notes on page 756 remove `TO` from the 'Underlined (required) words' list, and state explicitly that `TO` is NOT underlined (an optional word), matching the pattern already used on pp. 736/750/760/762 (e.g. "`AT` is not underlined", "`OF` is not underlined").

findings.pdf_says: Page 760 ends with 'Format 9 (program-pointer-assignment):' followed by the single syntax line 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO  identifier-8'. Nothing further is printed on page 760. Page 761 then OPENS with its own first line, the label 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):', above the Format 10 syntax diagram 'SET  { identifier-9 } ... { UP / DOWN } BY arithmetic-expression-3'.
findings.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md line 30846 (inside the page-760 slice, immediately before the anchor): 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8 Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):' -- and the page-761 slice then jumps straight into the fenced Format 10 diagram with NO label of its own.
findings.why_it_matters: The Format 10 label has been welded onto the end of the Format 9 syntax skeleton. Read literally, the Format 9 general format now appears to contain the trailing tokens 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):', which is not COBOL syntax and corrupts a general-format line; simultaneously the Format 10 diagram is left orphaned with no format label, so a reader (or a generator walking the page anchors) cannot tell which SET format the UP/DOWN BY diagram belongs to. Format 9 and Format 10 are distinct SET formats with different syntax rules and general rules.
findings.suggested_repair: Split line 30846 into 'SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8' (ending the page-760 content) and move 'Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):' to be the first content line AFTER the / '## Page 761' scaffolding and before the Format 10 fenced block, matching where it is printed. While there, consider fencing the Format 8 and Format 9 syntax lines (lines 30842 and 30846) in ``` blocks like every other SET format, so they are not mistaken for prose.

findings.pdf_says: '14.9.39.3   Syntax rules' is printed in exactly the same bold heading style and at the same outline depth as '14.9.39.1   General' and '14.9.39.2   General formats' on page 759 -- all three are fourth-level clause headings subordinate to '14.9.39  SET statement'.
findings.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md line 30946: '## 14.9.39.3 Syntax rules' (heading level 2), whereas its siblings are line 30738 '### 14.9.39.1 General' and line 30760 '### 14.9.39.2 General formats' (heading level 3), and their parent is line 30735 '## 14.9.39 SET statement' (heading level 2).
findings.why_it_matters: At level 2 the Syntax rules clause is promoted to a SIBLING of '14.9.39 SET statement' instead of a child of it, so any tool that builds a table of contents, resolves 'see 14.9.39.3', or extracts the rules belonging to the SET statement will detach the syntax rules from their statement. The same defect recurs at line 31157 ('## 14.9.39.4 General rules', page 763) and at lines 31494 / 31570 for 14.9.40.3 / 14.9.40.4, so the repair should be swept -- but only 14.9.39.3 falls on a page in this batch.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote line 30946 to '### 14.9.39.3 Syntax rules' to match its siblings, and sweep the .3/.4 subclause headings of the other 14.9.x statement sections for the identical promotion (14.9.38.4, 14.9.39.4, 14.9.40.3, 14.9.40.4 are already known instances).
